ws1.does_message_still_appear: No — it never appears to a user on v305. It is dead: defined at src/sutram_compiler.asm:680 ('Sutram truti: kosh-tarke kosh_push asamarthitam'), loaded only in .ge_call_koshpush_param_bad (lines 22440-22444), and no code jumps to that label (verified by grep — the only reference is its own label definition). Probed: parameter growth works with no message (11 22 99 3); slice storage refuses with E_KOSH_VIBHAG (not the old message); kosh_kship on a call result or a mala refuses with msg_kosh_required ('kosh prakriya hetu kosh-vitti avashyak', not the old message). No input tried produces 'asamarthitam'.
ws1.what_it_says: It still says 'Sutram truti: kosh-tarke kosh_push asamarthitam' (in the source and in the binary's data, dead) — wrong on both counts: old name (kosh_push, not kosh_kship) and describes a parameter-growth refusal that no longer exists (parameter growth now works and propagates). It is misleading for anyone reading the source (they would think the refusal still exists) but it does not lie to a student, because no student ever sees it.
ws1.what_it_should_say: It should say nothing — it should be deleted (msg_kosh_param_push line 680 and the dead label .ge_call_koshpush_param_bad lines 22440-22444), because parameter growth now works and there is no refusal to describe. No replacement message is needed: slice growth is already refused at slice storage (E_KOSH_VIBHAG, with a hint to pass the slice directly) and kosh_kship on a non-kosh is already refused with msg_kosh_required (correct, though generic). If a specific slice-growth message is wanted for the (now unreachable) kosh_kship-on-a-slice case, it should say (Sanskrit, current name, naming the case, with a hint): 'Sutram truti: vibhagah na vardhate — vibhagah drishtih eva, na svami; kosham eva vardhaya, tatah punah vibhagam kuru. Sanket: kosham eva preshaya (kosh k), athava vibhagam purvam anyatra pratilipya' — but since slice storage is refused first, this message would also be dead, so the clean action is the deletion.

ws2.kosh_param_grown_caller_reads: Yes — caller sees growth: 11 22 99 3 (value 99 and length 3). R129 ws1_paramgrow.sm, which refused on v302/v303, now compiles and runs on v305 (11 55, exit 0) — intended v304 behaviour change, not a regression.
ws2.kosh_param_grown_in_nested_block: Growth persists after the block closes; caller sees it. Mandapa block: a[1]=99, kosh_gan(a)=2. Yadi block: b[1]=88, kosh_gan(b)=2. No defect. (Probe note: the yadi flag parameter is dasham, not vitti — vitti is not a valid parameter type.)
ws2.next_gap: The slice-storage refusal is the next gap to decide on (not a defect — it is safe, but it is the broadest refusal in the new rules): it refuses storing a kosh slice in a vitti even when no growth ever follows, with a message that talks about growth ('if the kosh grows, its values go elsewhere') when no growth happens in the program at all. A user who writes 'vitti s = k[1:3]; likha(s[0])' (no growth anywhere) gets a refusal about growth, and the hint tells them to pass the slice directly (f(k[1:4])) — the right workaround, but the message does not say 'slices cannot be stored, only passed directly'. If the design intends slices to be pass-directly-only, the message should say that plainly and the reference should document it. If it intends slices to be storable when no growth follows, the compiler needs a narrower check (allow storage when it can prove no growth follows, or track the slice's source and refuse only the growth, not the storage). Owner's decision, not a Muse fix.
ws2.slice_no_hi_then_growth: At slice creation, yes — S2 fixed (verified 149/4: endpoint is the length after lo was evaluated, not before; see ws2_slice_s2). Across a later growth, the question is moot — you cannot hold a no-hi slice in a vitti (vitti s = k[2:] refuses with E_KOSH_VIBHAG, same as (c)), so there is no held slice whose endpoint could move after a later growth.
ws2.slice_param_directly_beside_growing_arg: No crash on v305 — refused at compile time in both variants (S1 closed). Call variant (use_slice(k[2:5], grow_it(k))): E_KOSH_VIBHAG, 'prakriya use_slice — kosh-vibhagah anyena ahvana-yuktena tarkena saha na diyate (tad ahvanam kosham vardhayet)' (a kosh slice is not given with another argument that has a call — that call might grow the kosh), with hint. Grow variant (may_grow(k[2:5], k)): E_KOSH_VIBHAG, 'prakriya may_grow koshan vardhayitum shaknoti — kosh-vibhagah tasyai na diyate (vriddhau tasya mulyani anyatra gacchanti)' (the prakriya can grow a kosh — a kosh slice is not given to it), with hint. (Probe note: vitti is not a valid parameter type, so the second parameter is dasham, not vitti.)
ws2.slice_s2_endpoint: Fixed — verified 149/4. Slice with omitted hi whose lo is a call that grows the kosh (k[grow_it(k):], grow_it pushes 99 and returns 1): first call yog=149 (slice k[1:4]=[20,30,99], sum 149 — if endpoint were the old length (3), sum would be 50); second call pankti_gan=4 (a second grow_it pushed another 99, length 5, slice k[1:5], length 4 — if endpoint were the old length (4), it would be 3). Endpoint is the length after lo was evaluated, not before (v305 fix in r23_gen_slice).
ws2.slice_then_growth: You cannot hold it — the compiler refuses to store a kosh slice in a vitti (E_KOSH_VIBHAG, 'kosh k vibhagah vittau na sthapyate — kosh vardhate cet tasya mulyani anyatra gacchanti', hint: pass the slice directly f(k[1:4]); in a vitti place only the kosh itself). Refusal is unconditional: vitti s = k[1:3] with NO growth after it at all is also refused with the same E_KOSH_VIBHAG. Safe (prevents a stale slice) but broader than S1 (refuses storage even when no growth follows). The expressible slice use — passed directly, used immediately, no growth in between — works (yog(k[2:5])=120, pankti_gan=3; yog(k[2:])=120, pankti_gan=3; hi exclusive, no-hi runs to end). So the brief's bullet as phrased has no expressible program on v305 — it is refused at the point you would try to hold the slice. That is itself the finding.
ws2.two_kosh_params_both_grown: Yes, both propagate: x[1]=99, y[1]=88, kosh_gan(x)=2, kosh_gan(y)=2.

ws3.decision: SIGN OFF for the compiler (Linux, v305) — yes, with polish. DO NOT SIGN OFF for v305 as a release (including Windows, installer, and IDE) — R132 and R133, in this same batch, name the blockers, and they must be fixed first.
not_signed_off_for: v305 as a release (including Windows, installer, and IDE) — R132: installer does not complete (wizard waits unbounded on a PowerShell that stalls after 'Copying Sutram files.'); two installations coexist with the older one winning on PATH, so a student typing 'sutram' gets an old version. R133: the OOM path crashes on Windows with 0xC0000005 and empty output instead of refusing as on Linux; the IDE leaves stale output on screen when a file is refused. These are release blockers, not compiler defects, and they stop a release even though the compiler is clean.
